newsitem.title: USA: Dow is denied delay in implant suit trial.
newsitem.headline: Dow is denied delay in implant suit trial.

text.p: A federal judge in Michigan denied a motion from Dow Chemical Co. and Dow Corning Corp. and allowed a Louisiana trial of a breast implant lawsuit to continue, the court said Tuesday.
The companies had asked U.S. District Judge Denise Page Hood in Detroit to stay her earlier ruling until they could ask the 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati to review it.
Hood ruled last week that the first two phases of a 9-week-old trial of a class-action lawsuit against Dow Chemical in Louisiana Civil District Court in New Orleans can proceed.

The Louisiana trial resumed Thursday. The trial had been halted by a May 8 ruling from the appeals court that all state and federal breast implant cases against Dow Chemical and Corning Inc. be consolidated in a federal court in Detroit.

Dow Chemical and Corning each own 50 percent of Dow Corning. Women suing the companies allege silicone gel breast implants made by Dow Corning have caused atypical connective tissue health problems. The companies deny the allegations.

Hood's latest ruling came Friday but was not released by the court until Tuesday. In denying the motion, Hood sided with the plaintiffs, who argue that the public interest for a timely resolution of the case would be harmed if a stay were granted.
"The plaintiffs are currently in trial and their right to a jury trial should not be further delayed," Hood wrote.
Dow spokesmen could not be reached for comment.
Dow Chemical stock was down 75 cents at $83.375 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
